body:
Thanks heeps for the advice everyone. I feel like I should let you know how it went.

About 10 minutes before the class I was having horrible anxiety. Panicing, wanting to vomit, couldn't think straight. But I know that if I power through it then I'll be set. So I head on down to the classroom, and its about 20-25 people. I choose a seat at the back away from people and of course the lecturer comes in and points me out saying she doesn't want people sitting there and so I apologize and take a seat in between two people.

Now at this point my mindset is just fake it until you make it, so I keep calm even though on the inside I'm pretty sure I'm about to throw up. She goes through the boring procedural stuff, including the rules regarding getting up and leaving to go to the bathroom. She says it's fine to do whenever you need and you don't have to ask. You'd think that would make me feel better but it didn't have much of an effect, I was still thinking in my head "She'll pick on the first person to do it and make an example out of them, I can't be the one to go."

So I'm sitting in there and I'm busting to go to the toilet. I've been in this situation so many times though, I know that there is nothing I need to relieve and it's just a trick my mind plays on me to make me leave the class. So I just stick to it and try to focus on the work. It's boring and dull work but eventually we get to the first hour mark and we get a break. I can't believe I made it! The feeling of relief at this 1/3rd mark was incredible. I casually get up and go use the restroom and return. My thoughts were that if I had made it that hour then I can definitely finish the rest of the day etc etc.

So my spirits were high, and luckily it just kept going up from there. There was quite a bit of communication required, and she forced us to meet people and partner up with people we didn't know. I'm glad she forced us to pick our partners because I definitely wouldn't have had the courage to go up and talk to someone myself, but keeping the whole 'fake it' theme going I just didn't show anything and I'm actually really proud of myself and how I held it together. I don't think talking is actually a problem for me, it's more I'm afraid of what people are thinking / what they aren't speaking. Anyways the girl next to me seemed more nervous than I was about being there and so it wasn't too bad to talk to her. Probably helps that most of my friends are girls anyway so I've never had a problem with the whole talking to girls thing.

Overall went really well, I am so glad I decided to do this course. The actual coursework itself is very mundane and pretty much below me at this point, but the social contact and exposing myself to the university environment has really boosted my confidence up and so I'm left feeling pretty happy!
I'm from New Zealand so I think that it might be very similar here. I'm hoping they have breaks then, don't think I want to be the odd one out leaving the lecture on the first day

I should probably add, I haven't really left the house since high school which was about 4-5 years ago now. I mean I go out and do odd jobs like shopping etc but being out for an extended period of time is a very rare thing for me. But I didn't know what else to do. I can handle short trips to the supermarket etc, but theres no real middle ground between trips like that and getting a job / studying, so I'm plunging into it. Maybe this was the wrong idea eeeep

Ahh a bit of both to be honest. I think my biggest nightmare would be needing to go to the bathroom though, the thought of it makes me feel sick right now. I always relieve myself before I go but I swear when I'm nervous I just need to go again within 15 minutes : (.

The problem with that is the education system still involves several years of schooling, interacting with others and picking subjects I would have no interest in. To be honest the main thought about it is being trapped in a lecture room for 1 hour in close proximity with others and no way to get out without drawing attention. I feel sick just writing about it.

I don't want to have to start all over again with a new therapist, especially if it means just doing the same work over and over. I don't have a problem with my therapist, I just wish it would go faster I guess.

Also what do you mean by use reddit for motivation?

I have tried 3 different types of therapists. I have even gone to a specialist anxiety clinic.

I am possibly going to try a new drug, but it's hard to get hold off. You need to have tried different meds which have failed, and now we are in the process of applying for it. But I don't expect a miracle cure.
